why: EOL-RELEASE-AN-1 (decided 2026-11-14): Microsoft supports accelerated networking on every Azure endorsed Linux distribution 'as long as the vendors don't mark them as end of life (EOL)' (accelerated-networking-overview, the section for machines with Mellanox adapters). data/supported-images.json goes by publisher and holds no release date, so each release the list admits has its STANDARD end of support here, read from the vendor's own page. Standard means the support every subscription gets: Canonical's standard security maintenance, Red Hat's Maintenance Support, SUSE's General support, Oracle's Premier Support, Debian's end of life (the end of support by the Debian security team), and the end of security support of AlmaLinux and Rocky Linux (their vendors give no support after it; review, 2026-11-15: a machine converted in place to AlmaLinux or Rocky Linux from an admitted image reports that release through the Azure Linux Agent). CentOS has no row: the scan refuses its image (OpenLogic, unsupported), so no admitted machine runs it. Each vendor also sells extended support (Ubuntu Pro ESM, Red Hat ELS, SUSE LTSS, Oracle Extended Support, Debian ELTS; Debian LTS is a volunteer project), so the product states the date and never calls the machine unsupported. The scan gives the warning linux-release-past-standard-support, and Checking stops the machine with linuxReleaseEndOfLife until an approver accepts it (onReleaseEndOfLife = proceed). Only the release the Azure Linux Agent reports is judged past a date: an image is the lowest release a machine can run. endOfStandardSupport is a day (YYYY-MM-DD) or, where the vendor gives only a month, a month (YYYY-MM): support ends at the end of that day or month. A null minor is every minor release of the major (the vendor dates the major). distroId is the os-release ID the release reader gives (Get-VmfLinuxRelease). A row with quote holds the words of the vendor page that give its date, read again on quotedUtc (review, 2026-11-15). The Debian LTS wiki shows the LTS schedule of Debian 12 from 2026-06-11; the release page of Debian 12, the vendor's own statement of the release, says full Debian support until July 11th, 2026, and that date is used.
watched: The drift check does not watch these pages: Canonical's page is built in the browser, Red Hat publishes its dates through an API whose answer carries the time it was made, and Oracle's is a PDF. EOL-DATES-WATCH-1 is the item that keeps this file current.
